questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a good university and close to nature; in particular the ocean and good surfing opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit tricky because you need your visa (which was delayed) to finish some of the things for uni

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up in the airport and dropped at campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Several; Koolobong, I-House and Campus East

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a well-equipped kitchen but there was also the option to be catered

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, but makes it very easy to get down there, get to know other people and it provides you with everything you need

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't miss anything, just wished that it had been a bit cheaper

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process itself went fairly easy and UOW is very helpful and accommodating with everything, but the process of getting the overseas student health cover (OSHC) and the visa is very crucial to stay on top with, since this ended up delaying up the whole proces for me and resulted in me having to reschedule my flight and arriving late

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just had to follow the instructions in the emails you received

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In all mails I have received some kind of contact from the university was provided that you could reach out to, and they were very quick at replying. After arrival the UPW helpdesk at uni was very helpful and available monday to friday and even for extended hours in the beginning of the semester

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not all of the courses I had initially seen was available, but I managed to get 4 of the classes that I wanted, so overall successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do the Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) with BUPA when you receive the mail about it, it's not worth it going around it, and apply for your visa before buying a plane ticket

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of the courses was at a lower level than what I have been used to, but all of the professors were very friendly and helpful

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Global Political Economy was both fun and challenging 
Overall the courses was a lot easier to pass than back home

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot less teaching in genereal; fewer lectures and tutorials and a lot more online. In particular lectures would be pre-recorded

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON216 - International Economics
ECON305 - Economic Policy
ECON315 - Macroeconomic Essential for Business III
POL309 - Global Political Economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Economics and Macro if you want courses that are not too timeconsuming and easy to pass

Global Political Economy if you are interested in a more critical approach towards economics and the history behind

Economic Policy if you want to know about the Australian Economic system

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up buying a car, because it made it a lot easier to go surfing and go on weekend trips

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and accommodation were both quite expensive and alcohol as well

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there is more than 100 clubs available at uni, both social, sports, cultural etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Something for everyone but you need to seek it out yourself

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Surfing and surf-camp, free run clubs, bouldering
Run clubs include: Good Energy Run Club (all girls club) and Never Lazy Run Club which can both be found on Instagram

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sea Cliff bridge for sunrise, hike mt. Keira, The Farm (great surf beach and stunning views), Seven Mile Beach and Jervis Bay, Sydney, Byron Bay, Tasmania, Melbourne, Cairns

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live on campus, go to surf-camp, join for 0-week and the parties, join some local activities like the run clubs, Wednesday uni nights in the bouldering centre etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendly, laid-back and open-minded culture and the outdoorsy style of living

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go surfing
Live on campus east if you want to surf
Take advantage of services uni has to offer

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is expensive but as an exchange I would definitely say worth it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to surf and meeting friends here, along with being at a university that was very invested in everyones' well-being and accommodating that

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a whole new school system, place and ways of doing academic stuff

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
